memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in." — Matthew 25:35

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
This is, as we know, the famous slogan of the Salvation Army: Soap, Soup, and Salvation. This Christian, zealous army of God carries a heavy burden for souls. They understood that to reach the heart, one must often first care for the body. They did not only pray; they acted. They gave themselves wholly to the cause, living entirely for the Army's mission.

Each member is a fighter, standing firm against Satan and his allies. They met bitter experiences wherever they went, facing rejection, hardship, and persecution. Yet, they remained unstoppable. In a very short period of time, they grew rapidly, expanding into more countries than anyone could have imagined. Why? Because they offered a holistic Gospel. First, SOAP, restoring human dignity to those covered in the grime of the streets. Second, SOUP, meeting the immediate physical hunger of the destitute. And finally, SALVATION, feeding the starving soul with the Bread of Life. They proved that the Church is not just a place of worship, but a barracks of soldiers ready to rescue the perishing.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "You cannot preach the Gospel to a man with an empty stomach." — William Booth

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, we thank You for the example of the Salvation Army and their unyielding zeal. Give us the strength to serve not just with words, but with action. Help us to see the needs of others—the need for dignity, the need for sustenance, and the need for You. Make us unstoppable in our love for the lost. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Do not underestimate the power of small acts of kindness. A cup of water, a warm meal, or a word of encouragement can be the open door through which Christ enters a heart. Be a soldier of compassion today.
